phase: Phase 8 E5d (fixed-data screen, written before any E5d run)
question: Does smoothing the learner (weight EMA, or a lower learning rate) reduce the per-generation value bias swings so that more generations pass the balanced gate?
data: E5 T self-play chunks + labels, gens 1-6 (benchmarks/reanalysis/e5/registry_T.json); init E4 candidate 52d1cbae; config configs/training/e5b_rl_T.yaml (balanced gate vs init)

groups.base: unchanged learner (seeds 7, 8 from E5c screen_base_s7/s8 + new seed 9)
groups.ema: candidate = EMA of learner weights, decay 0.99 (time constant 100 steps = 2/3 generation), seeds 7, 8, 9

rule: Over generations 2-6 of the 3 seeds (15 checks): proceed if (1) passes >= 8, (2) passes >= base + 4, (3) mean max(|bias_black|,|bias_white|) < base. If both proceed: more passes, then smaller bias. Generation 1 excluded (an EMA candidate still carries the init weights after 150 steps).
next_if_proceed: implement the chosen change in rl.loop (EMA: candidate = EMA, raw learner kept for resume), run T'' 6 generations (e5b_rl_T + change, balanced gate), then holdout v3 (seed 203) + paired A/B T'' best vs E4 candidate only if something is promoted
known_confound: Smoothing keeps candidates closer to the init model, which is also the gate reference; gate passes alone do not show strength. The SPRT in the T'' run is the strength check.
